summary: Downtown Charlottetown east of Great George: a tourist waterfront (Peake's Wharf's shingled shops and bar, Confederation Landing's bandstand, Founders' Hall's red-brick railway car shop, the port's teal-and-white cruise terminal), the old railway station (now WCB) and Brass Shop, the 2021 Epekwitk Mi'kmaq building with its glass corner drum, and inland a grid of painted 19th-century clapboard houses, The Great George's restored inn houses, the brick old convent (Sydney Boutique Inn) and Holland College's red-brick campus. Little has been built since 2020; the news is about what wasn't built (the Founders' lot, 199 Grafton) and what's coming down (Purity Dairy, Nov-Dec 2026).

buildings.name: Founders' Hall (Founders' Food Hall & Market), 6 Prince Street
buildings.facts: Built 1908 by E.A. Wallberg as the railway car shop (repaired rail cars). Became Founders' Hall, a Confederation exhibit run by CADC, which closed and sold it in 2017 to the port authority (Port Charlottetown). Port reopened the main floor as Founders' Food Hall & Market in Aug 2019 after delays (20+ vendors: Big Burger, Receiver Coffee, Stir It Up...). Closed March 2020 for COVID, reopened; open 7 days from July 2021. Vax-pass spot-check spat with two vendors, autumn 2021. Since summer 2024 the Downtown Charlottetown Farmers Market (Sundays) sets up nearby at Confederation Landing; its hot-food vendors were told no because the hall already has food businesses. City New Year's Eve party held there.
buildings.look: Two parts. Main hall: red-orange common brick (#8e4a36), two tall storeys (lidar top 9.8 m, eave 7.1), long side with five bays of very tall round-arched green-framed windows (dark green #2f5e4a frames, small panes) in two tiers, a weathered wood panel between tiers; raised tan stone sill/coping, a stepped/pointed gable parapet with cream stone coping over the centre bay carrying a blue-and-white square logo and 'FOUNDERS HALL / SALLE DES FONDATEURS' in cream letters; brick 'X' tie-plate ornaments between windows; short grey roof behind the parapet. Entrance block at the left end: a square flat-roofed tower clad in pink-salmon stucco/panel with a scored grid (#e5b39e), red coping band at top (#a8433a), brick arch panel on its face with a big arched window and 'FOUNDERS HALL / SALLE DES FONDATEURS' letters, green copper-coloured curved canopy (#5d8b7a) over glass double doors; newer signage on it reads 'Founders' Food Hall & Market' in script. A glass curtain-wall link (dark frames) joins tower to hall. Inside: exposed timber trusses, polished concrete, stalls clad in white shiplap and corrugated metal.

buildings.name: Port Charlottetown cruise terminal building (big unnamed 'retail' footprint by the cruise berth)
buildings.facts: Port Charlottetown (the harbour authority) runs the cruise terminal; a ~$5M terminal facelift (separate bus/taxi and truck entrances) and a second berth built 2019 so two ships can tie up. Records: 94 ship calls in 2024 (as many as 165,000 passengers scheduled), max four ships in a day; 2026 season opened in April with the Victory I, ~160,000 passengers expected. MSC Meraviglia (biggest ever) called Oct 2019. Sept 2025: three ships arrived in thick fog and woke the downtown with their horns. A 10-ft red-sand sculpture with 'PORT CHARLOTTETOWN' greeted passengers inside the terminal in 2023.
buildings.look: A long single-storey shed (lidar 6.8 m) along the wharf: white/very pale walls with a broad teal-green band (#2f8a78) at the base and around the doors, a darker green low-pitched or flat metal roof (#3d6b4f), rows of small windows and roll-up/glass doors. Inside it's open timber-framed like a market hall. Beside it on the wharf apron: a green steel gangway tower (a gantry with a stair and a bridge out to ships). The apron is wide grey concrete with yellow-painted bollards and edge kerb.

buildings.name: Lobster on the Wharf, 2 Prince Street
buildings.facts: Seafood restaurant and fish market on the wharf at the foot of Prince Street, seasonal, packed on cruise days (manager adds staff when ships are in, Aug 2025). July 2024: a family of four dined and dashed on a $170 bill; staff posted the security footage to Facebook. Kept a rare calico lobster in the market tank (2017). Stopped automatic straws (2018).

A large harbour-side deck with teal and yellow patio umbrellas and red chairs, grey wood decking. Gabled grey roof.

buildings.name: Peake's Quay Restaurant & Bar (Peakes Quay), foot of Great George Street
buildings.facts: On the old Peake's Wharf. Bought by the Dolan family in 1994 (also run the Charlottetown Yacht Club); restaurant & bar and a well-known dance bar. Public washroom on the ground floor costs the city ~$18K/yr to run (council question, June 2020). ~$300K site upgrade 2020-21. Marina has a floating food court (Nimrod's floating pizza bar, Zak's Burgers, The Chip Shack) since 2019 and rental floating cottages.
buildings.look: Two storeys (lidar 9.3 m), long, with a wraparound second-floor deck under a bright blue awning (#1f5fa8) and glass railings; walls in green-stained cedar shingle (#3f6e5c) with coral-red trim around doors and windows (#d8615a); several steep gabled roof sections with dark grey shingles, gable fronts facing the water, small cupola. Entrance under a little gabled canopy with an oval black board 'Peake's Quay Restaurant & Bar' in white with a boat drawing.

buildings.name: Confederation Landing Park bandstand (gazebo)
buildings.facts: Confederation Landing is the city's waterfront park (opened 1995), events venue for the 2014 150th; Sunday Downtown Farmers Market moved there from Queen Street in 2024 (set up round the park's oval). City revoked a permit for a MAGA-associated musician's concert there in 2025. Holodomor statue installed Sept 23, 2026.
buildings.look: Octagonal open bandstand on a raised stone platform: white round posts, a grey-shingled hipped/octagonal roof with a small square open lantern/cupola on top, cream-white trim. Wide curved stone steps (amphitheatre seating) step down in front of it to the lawn; an oval brick path loops the lawn.

buildings.name: Epekwitk Assembly of Councils building (Mi'kmaq Confederacy), Water & Hillsborough
buildings.facts: Built 2019-2020 ($3.6M-5.5M), opened January 2021; owned by Lennox Island and Abegweit First Nations. Mi'kmaq Confederacy of PEI on the 2nd floor, L'nuey on the 3rd, public ground floor for Indigenous art, culture and business (STEAM PEI ran programs there). The rounded corner room upstairs is the Assembly of Councils chamber with harbour views. OSM has it as an untagged footprint (id 1269123789 at the corner; verify).
buildings.look: Three storeys (lidar 15.3 m), dark red-brown brick (#7a3b2e) with a base of rough red sandstone/grey stone, and on the corner a tall rounded glass drum (curtain wall, dark frames) rising the full height, capped by a projecting round flat roof with a warm wood/copper soffit band (#b4703f); a section of charcoal panel cladding (#4a4d50) beside the drum; flat roof. Faces the Water/Hillsborough corner.

suggested._note: the corner tower is a round glass drum, not a square brick tower

buildings.name: Workers Compensation Board (the old Charlottetown railway station), Weymouth & Water
buildings.facts: Built 1907 by the railway (E.A. Wallberg), red PEI sandstone with Nova Scotia freestone trim; controversy at the time over the site (residents wanted the foot of Great George), cost overruns and allegations of corruption. Last passenger train 1969, CN left 1983, then a farmers' market, then empty; WCB bought it 1996 and restored it for its offices.
buildings.look: Two and a half storeys of rough red sandstone (#8a4636) with lighter freestone sills and quoins, a steep grey-slate hipped/mansard-like roof (#5d6266) with gabled dormers and tall sandstone chimneys, and a long low platform canopy (green-grey metal, on brackets) running along the track side and round the corner. Corner of Weymouth and Water.

buildings.facts: OSM draws a 909 m² outline here tagged building=no (not a building). current_events.what: Purity Dairy (est. Sept 1946, Kent Street) sold to ADL in 2023, empty since; people kept getting in; being stripped and demolished Nov-Dec 2026. Family keeps the land, 'no plans'. ADL also owns Perfection Foods: both downtown dairies now one co-op.

199 Grafton (parking lot behind the Polyclinic): 84-unit building approved June 2021 to be done Jan 2023; IRAC appeal, tax fight over 'affordable' units; developer upsized to 8 storeys/158 units Nov 2023 'to get about a 4.5 per cent return'; staff said no; owner pulled it Dec 2023 ('I'm all done'). Still a gated pay lot. Developer's claim: one apartment built below Euston for every 27 above.
Lot beside Founders' Hall: Jan 2020 plan for a 7-storey building with 48 micro-units of ~300 sq ft ('opening summer 2021'), still empty; OSM even tags its outline building=no.

Transitional housing: province converting its six-unit building on Hillsborough Street to 11 beds, 24-hour staff and an E-Watch camera; deferred twice, approved 7-2 June 2026; a no vote cited property values.

Cruise ships: record 94 calls in 2024; Sept 2025 three ships in fog blasted horns and woke downtown residents; 2026 season opened April with more ships but fewer passengers. Lobster on the Wharf adds staff on ship days; a $170 dine-and-dash there in July 2024 was solved by Facebook.
current_events.where: Port terminal 28325937, Lobster on the Wharf 28433989

current_events.what: Peake's Quay public washroom costs the city ~$18,000 a year to run (councillor asked why, June 2020).
Old convent turned 'five-star' inn and 22 luxury apartments for $8M+ (2017); the nuns 'would like to move back in', affordability 'still a question'.

Founders' Hall: CADC closed its Confederation exhibit and sold the building in 2017, the year of Canada's 150th; reopened as a food hall 2019; 2024 the Sunday market moved next door but its hot-food vendors were barred because the hall already sells food.
Charlottetown Inn dropped Best Western in 2016 because 'the Charlottetown name' was enough; sold to a B.C. company seven months later.
Province House reopened in autumn 2026 after nearly 12 years and ~$90M+ of conservation work (was due 2022).

8-storey, 85-unit apartment proposed June 2024 to replace 149-151 Great George at Kent (florist building beside Confederation Court Mall); sent toward public consultation. Status unknown. (West side of Great George; may belong to downtown_west.)
